newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico ended natgas imports Sept 2 - energy min.
newsitem.headline: Mexico ended natgas imports Sept 2 - energy min.

text.p: Mexico as of September 2 has stopped its natural gas imports, which were made necessary by an explosion in July at a gas processing plant, Energy Minister Jesus Reyes Heroles said Tuesday.
"I can inform you that as of yesterday we will have stopped importing gas because of the incident at the Cactus plant," Reyes told legislators.
An aide to Reyes said the minister was referring to natural gas. A Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) spokeswoman also confirmed that Mexico had halted natural gas imports as of September 2.
Mexico's situation with regard to propane gas was still not clear. The country has also been importing propane since the Cactus blast.
"$30 million was the impact of this incident with regard to required gas imports and what we stopped exporting," Reyes said.
Officials had originally said Mexico might have to import natural gas into early next year.
